title: Valid Palindrome
statement: A phrase is a palindrome if, after converting all uppercase letters into lowercase letters and removing all non-alphanumeric characters, it reads the same forward and backward.

examples.input: s = "A man, a plan, a canal: Panama"

hints: Use two pointers at start and end moving toward the middle.
Return false immediately if s[left] !== s[right].

solutions.title: Reverse String Compare
Two Pointers In-Place

input: A man, a plan, a canal: Panama
testCases.label: "A man, a plan..."

editorial.approach: Two pointers converging inward: place pointers at left = 0 and right = s.length - 1. Advance left and decrement right while characters are not alphanumeric. When both point to alphanumeric characters, compare them case-insensitively; if they differ, return false. Continue while left < right.
editorial.why_optimal: Operates in-place in O(n) time and O(1) auxiliary space without creating filtered intermediate string copies.
editorial.pitfalls: Failing to skip non-alphanumeric characters or skipping out-of-bounds when consecutive spaces/punctuations occur. Comparing characters before converting to lowercase.
